title: kate-ui: watch the open files and ask about a disk change
summary: kate-ui gains the notify crate on macOS. A watcher thread sends a message to the window when an open file changes on disk. The window runs Command::CheckDisk and shows the reload prompt sentence with two answers, Reload and Keep. Reload runs Command::Reload and Keep clears the flag.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. session.rs imports GPUI, the crate builds only on macOS, and the owner looks at the window after the change.

definitions.definition:
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
# FSEvents watcher for the open files. std has no file change notification.
notify = "8"

/// Start a watcher for `path` and send its path on the channel when the file changes.
fn watch_path(path: &std::path::Path, tx: std::sync::mpsc::Sender<std::path::PathBuf>) -> Option<notify::RecommendedWatcher>

/// The prompt sentence and whether a Reload answer exists, from the view's reload choice.
fn disk_prompt(ws: &Workspace, view: ViewId) -> Option<(&'static str, bool)>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add notify under the macOS target dependencies with the justification comment and run cargo update -p kate-ui so Cargo.lock gains the new crates only. Keep one watcher per open document path in a HashMap on WindowRoot. The reader side of the channel is polled from a GPUI timer every 500 ms; each path received runs Command::CheckDisk on the first view of that document. disk_prompt returns kate_core::document reload_prompt_line text for the document and true when the file state reload choice is Reload or Ask. When Some, the notice shows the sentence with the DiskAnswer buttons from notice.rs. Reload runs Command::Reload; Keep sets file.disk_change to None through a kate-core path that exists, or stores a keep flag on the window when none exists, and names that in the pull request. The test disk_prompt_is_none_for_a_clean_file opens a temp file and asserts disk_prompt is None, then writes other bytes to the file, runs CheckDisk, and asserts disk_prompt is Some with true. The owner edits an open file in another editor and sees the prompt. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: session::tests::disk_prompt_is_none_for_a_clean_file
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because disk_prompt does not exist. After the change a clean file has no prompt and a changed file has one with a Reload answer.
